dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical conjunction of two propositions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Combines the probability-measure, measurability, positivity, parameter-range, and failed-bound requirements, so every one of them must hold for the same witnesses.

dependency_coverage.name: Exists
dependency_coverage.meaning: Existential quantification over a type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Introduces, in order, witnesses mu, X, K3, and lam; each later witness may depend on all earlier witnesses.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The heterogeneous multiplication operation supplied by an HMul instance; here its arguments and result are real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Forms the real products lam * |X(x)| in the integrand and K3 * lam in the right-hand exponential.

dependency_coverage.name: InnerProductSpace.toNormedSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts a normed-space structure from an inner-product-space structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies typeclass structure needed to interpret the real-valued Bochner integral; it does not add a quantified object or logical condition.

dependency_coverage.name: Inv.inv
dependency_coverage.meaning: The inverse operation supplied by an Inv instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Interpreted with the real inverse instance, it produces K3^{-1} in the condition |lam| <= K3^{-1}.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: The non-strict order relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Interpreted using real order, it states both |lam| <= K3^{-1} and the exponential-integral bound that is then negated.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: The strict order relation supplied by an LT instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Interpreted using real order, it states 0 < K3.

dependency_coverage.name: Measurable
dependency_coverage.meaning: A function is measurable when inverse images of measurable target sets are measurable in its domain.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Requires X : Real -> Real to be Borel measurable with respect to the displayed measurable-space instances.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure
dependency_coverage.meaning: The proposition/typeclass asserting that a measure is a probability measure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Requires the witness mu to be a probability measure on the real Borel measurable space.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of measures on a type equipped with a measurable space.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes mu a measure on Real with its displayed measurable-space structure.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.integral
dependency_coverage.meaning: A real-valued Bochner integral of a function against a measure; the supplied one-level body is opaque and does not expose its behavior on non-integrable functions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Forms the integral of x |-> exp(lam * |X(x)|) with respect to mu. No integrability hypothesis is included, so the library's totalized-integral convention can affect the proposition in non-integrable cases.

dependency_coverage.name: NormedAddCommGroup.toSeminormedAddCommGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: Forgets part of a normed additive commutative group structure to obtain a seminormed additive commutative group structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides structural typeclass data for the real-valued integral and has no independent proposition-level content.

dependency_coverage.name: Not
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical negation, defined as implication to False.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Negates the non-strict exponential-integral upper bound; with real linear order this says the integral is strictly greater than exp(K3 * lam).

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Interprets a natural-number literal in a target type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Interprets the literal 0 as a real number in the positivity condition 0 < K3.

dependency_coverage.name: RCLike.toInnerProductSpaceReal
dependency_coverage.meaning: Provides a real inner-product-space structure on an RCLike scalar type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For Real, supplies typeclass structure used to construct the normed-space instance required by the integral; it adds no hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Fixes the sample space, values of X, and scalar witnesses K3 and lam all to be real-valued.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.exp
dependency_coverage.meaning: The real exponential function.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Appears pointwise as exp(lam * |X(x)|) under the integral and as exp(K3 * lam) on the right side of the failed inequality.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies real negation for absolute value and associated algebraic typeclass structure; it creates no extra binder or assumption.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instInv

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes Inv.inv K3 the real reciprocal 1/K3 in the admissible range for lam.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual non-strict order on real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLT

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instRCLike

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the real zero used in the strict positivity requirement on K3.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.lattice

dependency_coverage.name: Real.measurableSpace

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Fixes both the domain and codomain sigma-algebras for X and the measurable space on which mu is defined.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.normedAddCommGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: The normed additive commutative group structure on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the codomain structure needed for the real-valued Bochner integral; it adds no proposition-level condition.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: Builds the interpretation of the numeral 0 from a type's Zero instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Connects the numeral 0 to real zero in 0 < K3.

dependency_coverage.name: abs
dependency_coverage.meaning: Absolute value in a lattice-ordered additive group, defined as max(a, -a); here it is ordinary real absolute value.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Forms |lam| in the parameter restriction and |X(x)| inside the exponential integrand.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs homogeneous HMul from a multiplication instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Selects ordinary real multiplication for lam * |X(x)| and K3 * lam.

binders: There exists a measure mu on Real equipped with its Borel measurable space.
There exists a function X : Real -> Real, chosen after mu.
There exists a real number K3, chosen after mu and X.
There exists a real number lam, chosen after mu, X, and K3.
conclusions: The inequality integral exp(lam * |X(x)|) dmu(x) <= exp(K3 * lam) is false; equivalently in the real order, integral exp(lam * |X(x)|) dmu(x) > exp(K3 * lam).
mathematical_definitions: All appearances of Real use the usual real-number algebra and order.
The measurable structure on Real is its Borel sigma-algebra.
Absolute value is max(a, -a), hence ordinary real absolute value in this target.
The displayed integral is the real-valued Bochner integral against mu.
The products are ordinary real multiplication, exp is the real exponential, and K3^{-1} is the real reciprocal of K3.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There exist a probability measure mu on the Borel real line, a Borel-measurable real function X, a positive real constant K3, and a real parameter lam with |lam| <= 1/K3 such that the exponential moment integral of |X| at lam is strictly greater than exp(K3 * lam): integral_R exp(lam * |X(x)|) dmu(x) > exp(K3 * lam).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: This is purely existential: it asserts only that one tuple (mu, X, K3, lam) violating the bound exists; it does not quantify universally over probability spaces, random variables, scales, or admissible parameters.
The sample space is fixed to the real line with its Borel sigma-algebra, and X is a measurable self-map of that space.
No centering, independence, distributional assumption, moment condition, boundedness, or nonconstancy condition is imposed on X.

No Integrable hypothesis is imposed on x |-> exp(lam * |X(x)|). Because the integral operator is total while its non-integrable behavior is not exposed by the packet, non-integrable cases present a semantic/vacuity risk.
The condition |lam| <= 1/K3 permits lam to be negative, zero, or positive. The target does not require lam > 0 or lam != 0.
Since K3 > 0, its reciprocal is well-defined and positive; thus the parameter interval is nonempty.
At lam = 0, both exponential expressions are naturally 1 for a probability measure, so that value should not witness the strict failure; the proposition itself does not state this exclusion.
The right-hand side is exp(K3 * lam), not a lam-independent constant and not exp of a quadratic expression.
ambiguities: D011 exposes only an opaque one-level body for MeasureTheory.integral, so the packet does not determine the exact totalization convention when the integrand is not integrable. The translation therefore identifies the standard Bochner-integral role but cannot fully resolve the non-integrable case from the supplied dependency meaning.
